prediction.likelyOutcome: Lagoon is very likely to establish liability for breach and to recover the $364,212 in unpaid rent largely intact; frustration of purpose is a weak defense given the timeline. The accelerated/future-rent claim of $1,444,258 is legally sound in structure but faces a genuine, discovery-dependent mitigation dispute tied to the theater's redevelopment into a performance venue, making full recovery of that component on early summary judgment uncertain — expect either a partial summary judgment (liability and unpaid rent) with the accelerated-rent amount going to trial or further discovery, or a negotiated resolution somewhat below the full $1,808,470 demand.

issues.label: Liquidated Damages Clause as Unenforceable Penalty
Prematurity of Summary Judgment / Discovery Continuance

outcome.description: The district court granted Lagoon summary judgment in June 2022, held the liquidated-damages clause enforceable so that no mitigation was required, and (after Lagoon waived attorney fees) entered judgment for $1,808,470 plus costs. The Minnesota Court of Appeals reversed on December 11, 2023, holding the liquidated-damages clause unenforceable because actual damages were capable of estimation and the clause ignored the duty to mitigate, and remanded for further proceedings on actual damages and mitigation.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed (liquidated-damages clause unenforceable) and remanded; no final figure yet.
